topic: What is a token? How AI actually reads your words
title: AI Doesn't Read Words. It Reads Tokens.
description: Every chatbot splits your message into tokens before it reads it. Here's what a token is and why it decides your limits and costs.
sources: OpenAI Help Center: What are tokens and how to count them

scenes.heading: AI can't read words
scenes.narration: AI chatbots don't actually read your words. They read tokens.

scenes.heading: So what's a token?
scenes.body: A small chunk of text: a word, part of a word, or a symbol
scenes.narration: A token is a small chunk of text. Sometimes a whole word, sometimes part of one, sometimes just a comma.

scenes.heading: "unbelievable" →
scenes.narration: A long word like unbelievable can get split into pieces, like un, believ, and able.

scenes.label: characters per token in English
scenes.narration: In English, one token is roughly four characters, or about three quarters of a word.

scenes.heading: 100 English words ≈
scenes.narration: So a hundred words is around a hundred and thirty tokens.

scenes.heading: Why it matters
scenes.body: Chat limits, memory and API prices are counted in tokens
scenes.narration: And that matters, because chat limits, memory, and API pricing are all counted in tokens, not words.

scenes.heading: Tokens, not words
scenes.narration: Now you know how AI really reads. Follow for more tech, explained simply.
